body.en:
Question B-003-012-001.

Why the correct answer is right: Excessive SSB microphone gain overdrives the audio/RF chain, creating distortion and splatter that spreads into nearby frequencies.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It may cause harmonic interference on higher bands": Harmonics are multiples of the RF carrier and are controlled by transmitter filtering; microphone gain mainly causes adjacent splatter.
- sourceIndex 2: "It may cause interference to other stations operating on lower bands": Overdrive spreads around the operating frequency, not specifically to lower amateur bands.
- sourceIndex 3: "It may cause digital interference to computer equipment": Computer interference is an RF immunity or station-layout issue; high mic gain is about transmitted audio distortion and occupied bandwidth.
